title: Lesion atlas: left heart (aortic stenosis, HLHS, mitral, coarctation)

items.question: A screening scan shows asymmetric four chambers and an abnormal three-vessel view. Which group of lesions does the guideline suggest?
options: Progressive semilunar valve obstruction
Normal variant; no action
Atrial septal defect only
Venous anomalies only
items.explanation: Progressive semilunar obstruction is suspected when the three-vessel view is abnormal or the four chambers are asymmetric.

items.question: Fetal aortic stenosis with a poorly contracting left ventricle. The aortic valve velocity is low. What is the trap?
options: Valve Doppler may not reflect severity when left ventricular dysfunction is severe
A low velocity always means mild stenosis
Low velocity means the valve is normal
Velocity is the only measure that matters
items.explanation: Aortic valve Doppler may not reflect severity with severe LV dysfunction; reversed flow in the transverse arch predicts severe obstruction.

items.question: In aortic stenosis, which arch finding heralds critical obstruction at any gestation?
options: Retrograde flow in the arch on the side of the obstructed valve
Antegrade flow in the arch
A left-sided arch
A large thymus
items.explanation: Retrograde ipsilateral arch flow heralds critical obstruction; if absent at first, it should be looked for repeatedly.

items.question: Which features help judge severity and suitability for prenatal intervention in aortic stenosis?
options: Ventricular size, apex formation, hypertrophy, endocardial fibroelastosis and function
Fetal heart rate only
Nuchal translucency
Umbilical cord insertion
items.explanation: These ventricular features help judge severity and candidacy for prenatal intervention.

items.question: HLHS. A pulmonary venous forward-to-reverse VTI ratio below 3 predicts what?
options: Inadequate left atrial egress and greater likelihood of emergency atrial septoplasty in the newborn
A normal transition at birth
Complete heart block
Coarctation
items.explanation: A ratio below 3 predicts inadequate left atrial egress and a greater likelihood of emergency septoplasty.

items.question: HLHS with maternal hyperoxygenation testing late in pregnancy. Which result is associated with neonatal instability?
options: A fall of less than 10% in pulmonary artery pulsatility index
A fall of more than 10% in pulmonary artery pulsatility index
A rise in fetal heart rate
No change in umbilical artery flow
items.explanation: Lack of vasoreactivity (a fall of less than 10% in branch PA pulsatility index) is associated with neonatal instability and urgent atrial septal opening.

items.question: The left heart looks small and the foramen ovale appears restrictive, with no other heart disease. What does the guideline warn?
options: Isolated foramen restriction may make left structures look small with no consequence after birth
This is always hypoplastic left heart syndrome
Immediate delivery is needed
The finding has no relevance at all
items.explanation: In isolation, foramen ovale restriction can make left-sided structures appear smaller but have no consequence after delivery.

items.question: Mild mitral regurgitation is seen in a fetus. How should it be regarded?
options: As abnormal; and consider left ventricular outflow obstruction
As a normal finding
As normal unless the heart rate is low
As an artefact of colour gain
items.explanation: Any degree of fetal mitral regurgitation is abnormal; with mitral regurgitation, consider associated LV outflow obstruction.

items.question: Mitral stenosis. Which finding is critical in judging whether the mitral valve is adequate?
options: Direction of flow at the foramen ovale
Fetal heart rate
Cardiac axis
Thymus size
items.explanation: Flow direction at the foramen ovale is critical in judging adequacy of the mitral valve.

items.question: Which set of findings suggests coarctation?
options: Right ventricle larger than left, ascending aorta smaller than the superior vena cava, small arch and isthmus
Left ventricle larger than right with a dilated ascending aorta
Normal four chambers with a large isthmus
Pericardial effusion only
items.explanation: These are the coarctation findings listed in Table 13.

items.question: A colleague says a prenatal diagnosis of coarctation is reliable. What does the guideline say?
options: It has substantial false-positive and false-negative rates
It is never wrong
It has false positives but no false negatives
It is reliable if the heart rate is normal
items.explanation: Prenatal diagnosis of coarctation has substantial false-positive and false-negative rates.
